message:
fix(host,viewer): keep the provenance signal across a failed encode; retire tombstones on a boundary, not a clock; throttle the deferred-resync line by time

Codex's final review found three real gaps in the previous two commits.

The stage returns early when encode_frame_surface is rejected or encode_frame_bgra fails, both of
them before the provenance check. An encode can fail after the MFT has accepted the input, so that
call may be the one that overflowed the FIFO -- and with no pending request the tick retry had
nothing to retry, leaving the gate open on an encoder whose output order is undescribed.
EncoderState::NoteProvenance now records it at every exit from the encode call.

The tombstone expired after 5 s, so a host that kept resending the abandoned AU for longer got it
re-assembled and abandoned a second time -- the boundary the previous commit was meant to close.
Retirement is now by meaning, not by clock: when delivery has passed that seq in its generation
(the ordinary stale guard covers it from then on), when a delivery of another generation makes the
old seq space irrelevant, on Reset, or at the capacity bound. The bound's cost -- sixteen heads
abandoned with no delivery between them -- is written down where it is enforced.

The deferred-resync log used a failure count that a spent budget never increments, so it printed
every frame while the window ran out; it is throttled by time now.

Regressions: the shared-core tombstone unit covers the new boundaries (still held after 10 s with
no delivery, retired once delivery passes it or another generation arrives, capacity, Reset), and
epoch test [4] adds the wiring case (NoteProvenance idempotent, everything refused while latched,
a spent budget keeps the request pending without counting a failure, the next window succeeds).
The early-return call sites themselves are covered by reading, not by an executed test: the
encoder has no transform-injection seam to force an overflow with. history #420.
